files.source.svg: author source SVG (from the paper's arXiv/source bundle)
files.preview.png: PNG render of the author SVG
files.print.png: the figure as extracted from the published PDF, at print size
files.semantics.json: full semantic record for this figure

templates.why_chosen: Stacked (not side-by-side) comparison joined by an explicit 'V.S.' divider, with a dashed bracket naming the paper's scope.
templates.what_to_learn: Stack the two designs vertically when each is wide; a centred 'V.S.' label plus a dashed 'focus of this paper' bracket replaces sub-captions.

templates.why_chosen: Star, high-confidence nested-stack exemplar: each Compute Node and Memory Node box nests a NIC box that itself nests a three-level protocol stack, MAC and PHY, mirrored on both sides of a V.S. comparison.
templates.what_to_learn: Draw a protocol stack as boxes literally inside the NIC box that owns it, one level per layer, and repeat the identical nest on both compute and memory nodes so a labelled dashed bracket can span just the layers that are the paper's actual focus.

templates.why_chosen: Uses the literal V.S. rule for wide halves: a compact one-line baseline stacked over a wider two-node Ethernet Fabric design, with the paper's contribution named in orange text and bracketed rather than boxed.
templates.what_to_learn: When one half is much simpler than the other, stack them top-to-bottom with a horizontal V.S. rule instead of forcing equal-width side-by-side panels, and name the paper's scope with a coloured label plus dashed bracket rather than a boxed outline.
